subject.title: Dashboard shows deployment version drift warning

question: Should ClawHub treat frontend/backend build-SHA drift as an actionable production warning, or as an expected state for backend-only and frontend-only deploy targets?
rationale: Current code and tests intentionally warn on unequal SHAs, while the deploy workflow allows partial deploys; automation cannot choose whether to preserve the strict contract or change the warning policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Keep Strict Same-SHA Contract
options.body: Keep the warning semantics and fix production/deploy stamping so coordinated deploys always expose matching frontend and Convex SHAs.

options.title: Make Partial Drift Expected
options.body: Document backend-only and frontend-only deploy drift as normal, then downgrade or reword the banner and tests so only actionable skew looks alarming.

options.title: Disable The Drift Warning
options.body: Remove or suppress the banner, accepting that operators lose an existing signal for real frontend/backend deployment skew.

recommendation.title: Keep Strict Same-SHA Contract
recommendation.body: Keep the warning semantics and fix production/deploy stamping so coordinated deploys always expose matching frontend and Convex SHAs.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is the strongest routing candidate from current-line blame and CODEOWNERS for the deploy documentation surface.
